games.title: Final Fantasy IV
games.note: Hiroyuki Ito designed its Active Time Battle system after watching Formula One cars pass each other.

games.title: Final Fantasy V
games.note: Its job system lets characters carry abilities between classes such as Knight, Thief and Black Mage.

games.title: Final Fantasy Adventure
games.note: Released in Japan as Seiken Densetsu: Final Fantasy Gaiden, it started the Mana series.

games.title: Secret of Mana
games.note: Up to three people can play at once; its ring menu pauses the action to pick items and spells.

games.title: Chrono Trigger
games.note: Made by a 'Dream Team' of Hironobu Sakaguchi, Yuji Horii and Akira Toriyama; it has more than ten endings.

games.title: Chrono Cross
games.note: Written and directed by Masato Kato, who reworked parts of his Satellaview side story Radical Dreamers.

games.title: Illusion of Gaia
games.note: The hero, Will, travels through versions of real ancient sites such as the Great Wall and Angkor Wat.

games.title: Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars
games.note: Square developed it with Nintendo, with Shigeru Miyamoto as producer.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts
games.note: Tetsuya Nomura's debut as a director, mixing Disney worlds with Final Fantasy characters.

games.title: Alone in the Dark
games.note: Put polygon characters on pre-drawn backgrounds, the format Resident Evil later used.

games.title: Final Fantasy Tactics
games.note: Yasumi Matsuno created Ivalice for it, a world he reused in Vagrant Story and Final Fantasy XII.

games.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together
games.note: Yasumi Matsuno's war story, where choices split the plot into different paths.

games.title: Vagrant Story
games.note: Matsuno's dungeon-crawling action RPG; its art style and Ivalice setting carried over into Final Fantasy XII.

games.title: Famicom Wars
games.note: A Japan-only turn-based war game; its series reached the West as Advance Wars in 2001.

games.title: Fire Emblem Awakening
games.note: Planned as a possible final entry if it sold poorly; its success revived the series.

games.title: Final Fantasy XI
games.note: PC and PlayStation 2 players shared the same servers, an early cross-platform online world.

games.title: Final Fantasy XVI
games.note: Its political story drew on the early seasons of Game of Thrones.

games.title: Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light
games.note: Produced by Tomoya Asano; a planned sequel became Bravely Default.

games.title: Bravely Default
games.note: Brave lets you spend future turns now; Default saves turns for later.

games.title: Octopath Traveler
games.note: Introduced the HD-2D look: pixel-art sprites in 3D scenes with modern lighting.

games.title: Triangle Strategy
games.note: Party members vote on major decisions using the Scales of Conviction.

games.title: Final Fantasy XIII-2
games.note: Its Historia Crux map lets players jump between eras and alternate timelines.

games.title: Stranger of Paradise: Final Fantasy Origin
games.note: A dark reimagining of the first Final Fantasy, conceived by Tetsuya Nomura.

games.title: Lost Odyssey
games.note: Hironobu Sakaguchi's tale of an immortal soldier, with short stories by novelist Kiyoshi Shigematsu.

games.title: Blue Dragon
games.note: Reunited Hironobu Sakaguchi, Akira Toriyama and composer Nobuo Uematsu.

games.title: Xenogears
games.note: Began as Tetsuya Takahashi and Kaori Tanaka's rejected pitch for Final Fantasy VII.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles
games.note: Set on the bodies of two frozen giant gods; a fan campaign helped bring it to North America.

games.title: Sea of Stars
games.note: Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda wrote several of its tracks.

games.title: The Messenger
games.note: Shifts from 8-bit to 16-bit graphics and sound when you travel through time.

games.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
games.note: The first game from Sandfall Interactive, a small Montpellier studio founded by former Ubisoft developer Guillaume Broche.

games.title: Suikoden
games.note: Loosely based on the Chinese novel Water Margin; you recruit 108 Stars of Destiny to your army.

games.title: Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes
games.note: Crowdfunded on Kickstarter in 2020 by Suikoden creator Yoshitaka Murayama, who died shortly before release.

games.title: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals
games.note: Its dungeons are full of block and switch puzzles, plus a 99-floor random Ancient Cave.
